plans.note: Section 9 is the express limitation of liability; check mutuality, cap amount/formula and carve-outs (indemnity in sec-8-2, confidentiality in sec-10). Confirm the warranty disclaimer in sec-8 does not compound the cap.

Section 8 (INDEMNIFICATION) should carry Commerce One's third-party IP indemnity in favour of Corio as licensee/host; check whether Corio's reciprocal indemnity (including for hosting or trademark use under sec-6) is broader than defensive, and whether the sec-9 cap swallows it.

Look for field-of-use or market restrictions tied to CORIO MARKET SEGMENT / TERRITORY in the grant of rights (sec-3), shared resources (sec-13) and the sales and marketing cooperation exhibit (sec-20/sec-p0197). Flag only restraints on Corio's own business or competing products.

Check the grant of rights and the marketing cooperation exhibit for any obligation on Corio to source hosting/procurement software exclusively from Commerce One or to refrain from other ASP offerings.

Pricing and revenue-sharing exhibits are the only plausible home for a most-favoured-pricing or best-terms clause; an MFN running in Corio's favour is acceptable and should not be flagged. May well be absent.

No dedicated personnel clause in the outline; if a non-solicit exists it would sit in miscellaneous (sec-14) or alongside shared resources/support staffing (sec-13, sec-5). Verify before recording as missing — a mutual, time-limited restraint would be acceptable.

Section 11 governs term and termination; confirm Corio has a convenience exit on notice without penalty and that Commerce One cannot terminate at will mid-term. Cross-check any termination fees or accelerated payments in sec-4/sec-17.
Initial term, auto-renewal and non-renewal notice window should appear in sec-11; check the pricing exhibit for renewal uplifts (an uncapped uplift is a rationale note, not a standalone deviation).
Governing law, venue and any arbitration reference (note the defined term RULES) should sit in miscellaneous; California courts would be an accepted law.
Assignment/change-of-control provision expected in sec-14; confirm Corio may assign to affiliates and successors and that Commerce One has no termination right on Corio's change of control.

Ownership sits in the grant of rights and the DEVELOPMENTS / EMPLOYEE NDA-INVENTION definitions; check whether Corio-created developments, configurations or Customer data are assigned to Commerce One, and confirm sec-10 protects Corio data.

Section 2 (GRANT OF RIGHTS, id sec-3) plus the SOFTWARE/DEMONSTRATION SOFTWARE exhibit define scope; verify the licence is non-revocable at will and extends to Corio affiliates, contractors and its hosted CUSTOMERS/SOFTWARE USERS in the TERRITORY.
Any right for Commerce One to audit Corio's books, servers or user counts would sit in FEES or the payment-terms exhibit; test for notice, frequency, off-site records review and vendor-borne cost.

Check payment terms for late-payment penalties or liquidated sums payable by Corio; service credits or support commitments running in Corio's favour under Exhibit C are beneficial and should not be flagged.

Section 7 (WARRANTIES AND DISCLAIMER, id sec-8) with the defined Warranty Period and Acceptance Test; assess duration and whether the remedy is a real repair/replace or refund rather than disclaimer-only.
No insurance heading in the outline; scan miscellaneous and the indemnity section before recording as missing, given Commerce One personnel may touch hosted environments.
Look for minimum licence/revenue-share commitments, guaranteed IMPLEMENTATION FEE or minimum seat counts in FEES and the pricing exhibit; a take-or-pay without an exit is the concern.

Post-termination effects should be in sec-11, supplemented by the source code escrow in sec-12; confirm continuity for hosted CUSTOMERS, return/deletion of data and migration assistance rather than immediate cessation.
